subject: Mutual action plan: pilot MAP + GPU pool sizing & lead times
messages:
From: Jordan Miller <jmiller@medsight.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot capacity needs + timeline for MAP

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. MediSight is keen to run a 6-week pilot that will exercise our HL7 ingestion + anonymized clinical prompt set. High level asks:

- Target peak concurrent requests: ~120 r/s for generation workloads (mostly chat + extractors).
- Expected average sequence length ~1,200 tokens (with spiky 3k token cases during long reports).
- Ramping plan: week 1-2 smoke, week 3-4 load test (50% target), week 5-6 production-like run.

We need a MAP that lays out evaluation gating, SLA expectations, and procurement milestones — especially any lead times for Dedicated or Private GPU pool reservations so we can align procurement and legal. Can you propose a schedule with suggested GPU pool sizing and acceptance criteria?

Also looping in procurement (procurement@medsight.com) to bake in contract and payment cadence.

Best,
Jordan
Director of Product
MediSight Health

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jmiller@medsight.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity needs + timeline for MAP

Jordan — thanks for the clear requirements. Attached is an initial MAP workbook (mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx) and a proposed GPU tranche schedule (proposed-gpu-tranche-schedule.csv). High-level summary below; full details are on tab "MAP-summary" in the workbook.

Key proposal (short):
- Pilot footprint: reserve a 16-GPU A100e-ish pool (quantized LLM execution) with continuous batching + KV-prefix cache enabled. Equivalent throughput expected: ~100–140 r/s depending on batching window.
- Safety hedge: reserve a second 8-GPU flex tranche to be activated as burst capacity during week 4–6 if 95th percentile latency increases >30% vs baseline.
- Lead times: for Dedicated pools we recommend a 6–8 week procurement window for guaranteed tranche procurement and capacity carve-outs (hardware and placement). For Private on-prem deployments we estimate 10–14 weeks (hardware + on-site acceptance) unless using an existing customer-managed cluster.
- Evaluation plan: 6-week cadence matching your outline. Acceptance criteria include 95th percentile token latency under 450ms for chat tails and stable end-to-end P95 SLA for the extractor pipeline under defined dataset (see MAP QC tab).

Action items I propose for the MAP with owners and target dates:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope + sign MSA addendum (owner: Procurement / Redwood Sales).
- +2 weeks: contract countersigned, deposit invoiced for tranche 1 (owner: MediSight Procurement).
- +4 weeks: tranche 1 reserved & canary environment provisioned (owner: Redwood Infra).
- +6 weeks: pilot run begins (owner: MediSight & Redwood Eng).
- +12 weeks: decision checkpoint to convert to Dedicated reservation or extend Private deployment.

I'll set up a short sync to walk through the workbook tomorrow. Ben — can you confirm the expected throughput numbers on the 16 GPU config and sanity-check latency assumptions? Tessa — procurement template and billing cadence please; Jordan I'll queue procurement notes for your team.

Thanks,
Priya
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Jordan Miller <jmiller@medsight.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-06T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity needs + timeline for MAP

Quick sanity check on the sizing — ran a small sim against our quantized M-family runtimes. Notes:

- 16x A100-equivalent (q4_0 profile) with batching window tuned to 20–30ms and KV prefix cache gives ~115 r/s sustained for 1,200-token median sequences. Peak bursts hit ~170 r/s for short sequences.
- 95th-percentile tail latency (chat) estimated 380–480ms depending on tokenization behavior; the 450ms P95 target is achievable with the burst tranche available.
- If MediSight expects heavier long-sequence distribution (>2k median), recommend moving the baseline to 24 GPUs or increasing the batching--but that will raise unit cost ~18%.

I'll add a small "stress scenarios" sheet to the MAP workbook showing cost delta vs pool size. Also included a note on quantization tradeoffs (q4_0 vs q8_0) for accuracy-sensitive extractors.

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: stress-scenarios-summary.md)

From: Ops Procurement <procurement@medsight.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Miller <jmiller@medsight.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity needs + timeline for MAP

Hi Priya / Ben — thanks for the workbook. A few procurement/contract questions to be explicit in the MAP so our sourcing team can greenlight: 

1) Payment cadence: deposit required before tranche reservation — please confirm deposit amount as % of first-month committed capacity and whether refundable if the pilot fails acceptance.
2) SLA credits and early termination terms during pilot window.
3) Data residency / SOC2 evidence; we will need SOC2 artifacts while evaluating Private deployment options.

Our target: have a countersigned addendum and deposit wired by 2026-08-20 to meet the +4 week provisioning target. If lead times are longer, we need to know now so we can prioritize Dedicated vs Hosted.

Procurement (MediSight)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Procurement <procurement@medsight.com>
Cc: Jordan Miller <jmiller@medsight.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity needs + timeline for MAP (notes + next steps)

Procurement team — quick responses inline and next steps below.

1) Deposit: Standard tranche deposit is 25% of the first 3 months' committed spend for Dedicated reservations. For pilots we can offer a refundable 15% pilot credit if the MAP acceptance criteria are not met during the six-week window (exceptions apply — see MAP workbook tab "Commercials").

2) SLA / early termination: Pilot addendum will include a 30-day early termination window with prorated credit for unused committed capacity; SLA credits default to service credits applied per the MSA. I'll attach a draft addendum to the Drive link; legal is willing to fast-track if procurement provides a standard PO.

3) SOC2 / evidence: attaching a snapshot SOC2-snapshot.pdf and a short evidence guide in the Drive folder. For Private on-prem we require completion of the Network & Acceptances checklist (in the MAP workbook) prior to go-live; that typically contributes to the longer 10–14 week lead time.

Next steps (owners & dates):
- 2026-08-13: sync (30m) to review MAP Workbook — Priya / Ben / Jordan / Procurement.
- 2026-08-18: countersign MSA addendum + issue PO (owner: MediSight Procurement).
- 2026-08-25: tranche 1 reservation confirmed & invoice issued (owner: Redwood Billing).
- 2026-09-01: canary provisioning complete (owner: Redwood Infra).

Jordan — if those dates look good I'll lock them in and update the MAP workbook with the procurement-specific checklist.

Thanks,
Priya
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
(attachments: mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx; SOC2-snapshot.pdf)
